title: The kth value of an insertion sort
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered set, let $l$ be a list of elements of $\alpha$, and let $k$ be a natural number with $1\le k\le |l|$. The element at zero-based position $k-1$ in the list obtained by sorting $l$ into nondecreasing order by insertion sort satisfies the defining rank conditions for being the $k$th smallest element of $l$: it occurs in $l$, fewer than $k$ entries are strictly smaller, and at least $k$ entries are at most it.
